rows.en: <operator(10010,1)><speed(2)>Once this operation's done, I guess it's goodbye to everyone.
<operator(17020,1)><speed(2)>You all looked out for us in more ways than I can count.
<operator(25010,1)><speed(2)>Even once we're both back home, we've still got work waiting for us.
<operator(23030,1)><speed(2)>Just fighting alongside us this far was enough. We'll handle the rest ourselves.
<operator(17040,1)><speed(2)>I'm grateful to you all, truly. I won't ever forget this.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Faye<ce()>... what kind of man was <color(5)>Berkt<ce()>, really?
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>He was a man who almost never let his thoughts show.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>He hid his face, so I never knew he was <color(4)>Barrel<ce()>. I was only carrying out my orders.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>But he was a man who felt utterly ruthless, willing to do anything for his goal, and full of a bottomless hatred.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>He... found out I exist. That someone exactly like him is out there, in a world different from his own.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>And he came to hate me for it.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>I don't know why, but... I have to see this through to the end.
<operator(17040,1)><speed(2)>You're the real key to this operation. I'm counting on you... <color(4)>Barrel<ce()>.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>I don't even know his face, but... something my own father made is behind all of this.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>I will stop it, whatever it takes.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Barrel<ce()>, don't shoulder all of it yourself. None of this is your fault.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>It's a problem only I can solve. And I've already decided to stop <color(5)>Berkt<ce()>. So I want to see it through.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Barrel<ce()>...
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>By the way, <color(4)>Faye<ce()>, you... you have to leave the ship.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>Why?
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>Because the moment the <color(6)>Baldora Drive<ce()> shuts down, we'll have to cross the wormhole right away.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>If you're with me... you'll end up back in the other world. You belong here, don't you?
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>I'm not leaving.
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>Even if it means I can never come back... I want to see my responsibility through.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Faye<ce()>... are you sure about this?
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>If I'm not aboard, it'll hold up the operation. There's no other way.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>But you can never come back again, you know that?
<operator(1060,1)><speed(2)>That's fine. I'm still worried about you, <color(4)>Barrel<ce()>.
<operator(1040,1)><speed(2)>All right... I'm counting on you, <color(4)>Faye<ce()>.
<operator(23030,2)><speed(2)>Thanks for everything. Hope you make it home safe.
<operator(5010,1)><speed(2)>I'll get back no matter what. <color(5)>Char<ce()>'s bound to pull something. I can't rest easy leaving it like this.
<operator(23030,1)><speed(2)>Same goes for me. This doesn't put an end to the Limit of Questions.
rows.notes: 'Limit of Questions' = locked rendering of Kudan no Genkai (encyclopedia_022 text id 77).

rows.en: <operator(5010,1)><speed(2)>Heh... seems we're both already thinking ahead. But first, we need to finish this.
<operator(23030,2)><speed(2)>Yeah. Let's go.
<operator(25010,2)><speed(2)>It's finally coming to an end. Still, not crushing the <color(5)>New Federation<ce()> is one regret.
<operator(17020,1)><speed(2)>Then why not simply stay on this side?
<operator(25020,1)><speed(2)>Don't kid around. I have to settle things with this guy.
<operator(19020,2)><speed(2)>But that side looks easy to live in. Kind of envious, honestly.
<operator(14030,1)><speed(2)>Oh! So, you coming, then? We'll roll out the welcome mat!
<operator(19020,2)><speed(2)>Kidding, only kidding! Still... I like it better on this side.
<operator(14010,1)><speed(2)>In the end, everybody loves their own world best, huh.
<operator(19010,1)><speed(2)>Yeah... that's why this is the last of it.
<operator(17010,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Barrel<ce()>... guess this is goodbye.
<operator(21010,1)><speed(2)>It was a short while, but it's a shame to see it end.
<operator(1040,2)><speed(2)>I'm glad I got to meet you all too.
<operator(23010,2)><speed(2)>Same here. I'll never forget it.
<operator(10030,1)><speed(2)>Still, with our numbers thinned out, I wonder if we'll manage from here.
<operator(23100,1)><speed(2)>Yeah, I know. It's going to get rough for both of us.
<operator(10010,1)><speed(2)>Guess we got used to having such a big crew.
<operator(17040,1)><speed(2)>Everyone's grown plenty dependable. <color(4)>Garrod<ce()> and <color(4)>Renton<ce()> especially have come a surprisingly long way.
<operator(23040,2)><speed(2)>That's right. So we've got to send them off with confidence.
<operator(10020,1)><speed(2)>But saying goodbye to this many machines really is a waste, huh...
<operator(12031,2)><speed(2)>We'll be fine. So this is the last of this dream team-up, then.
<operator(17030,2)><speed(2)>Hey... if you're up for it, why not stay here? And then, you and me...
<operator(1020,1)><speed(2)>No kidding around today. When he shows up, we have to stop him, no matter what...
<operator(17030,1)><speed(2)>Ugh, that's cold...
<operator(21020,2)><speed(2)>Don't let it get to you, I got shot down too.
<operator(12061,1)><speed(2)>Tough luck~.
<operator(12071,1)><speed(2)>Rest in peace~.
rows.notes: 'Namu~' (Buddhist chant for the dead) used as a mock condolence for the rejected suitor; rendered idiomatically.

rows.en: <operator(1020,2)><speed(2)>But... thank you, for everything. Let's move out.
<operator(12051,1)><speed(2)>Not every day you get an experience like that.
<operator(12061,1)><speed(2)>Seriously, seriously. Perfect material for a manga.
<operator(12071,1)><speed(2)>Maybe not being able to go home would make for even better material...
<operator(12051,2)><speed(2)>Don't go cursing it like that!
<operator(19050,1)><speed(2)><color(4)>Ryoma<ce()>, I'm counting on you. See them off for me.
<operator(19040,1)><speed(2)>Yeah, leave it to me. Time I paid back all the debts I've racked up so far.
<operator(16010,1)><speed(2)>I'm heading back to Iwakuni... And someday I'll see everyone again!
rows.notes: 'Iwakuni' = real-world place name (Asap Suzuki's hometown), not a glossary term.

rows.en: <operator(16040,2)><speed(2)>Yes, <color(4)>Asap<ce()>. I'm coming with you!
<operator(12031,1)><speed(2)>...
<operator(12011,1)><speed(2)>What's wrong, <color(4)>Ruri<ce()>?
<operator(12031,1)><speed(2)>I only have a bit of a bad feeling...
<operator(12011,1)><speed(2)>It's fine. We'll make it back for sure...
<operator(12031,2)><speed(2)>That's true. <color(4)>Yurika<ce()>'s waiting for us too, after all.

uncertainties.issue: 'New Federation' kept per orchestrator lock even though Isamu (Macross Plus) is speaking of an in-fiction political body foreign to his own series; matches how the term is used elsewhere for the crossover-world antagonist faction.

Table 0 slot 39: source katakana is 'Barudona Doraibu' (バルドナ・ドライブ), matching glossary.json term.baldora_drive's ja reading exactly; 'Baldora Drive' is the correct locked rendering here, not the separate person 'Dr. Bardona'/'Jill Bardona'. Accepted.

Table 0 slot 22 'I'm still worried about you, Barrel' for a line naming Barrel in third person while speaking directly to him is the established direct-address convention seen throughout the corpus; not an invented addressee.
Table 1 slot 224: '南無～' rendered 'Rest in peace~' as a mock condolence for the rejected suitor - per orchestrator ruling, this rendering is fine and is kept unchanged.

Table 1 slot 100 uncertainty: 'New Federation' kept for Isamu's line per the orchestrator's project-wide lock, even though he (a Macross Plus character) is referring to the crossover-world antagonist faction rather than a body native to his own series; this is consistent with how the term is used elsewhere in the corpus for that same faction. Accepted.
'-chan'/'-san' dropped on Ruri (slot 380) and Yurika (slot 383), consistent with established corpus practice.
No mistranslations, reversed meanings, wrong addressees/subjects, or misplaced commands found; all <operator>/<speed>/<color>/<ce> tags match the source in content and order.
